title: Character & Conduct
description: A question bank on honesty, justice, mercy, responsible speech, family and neighbour rights, and ethical conduct in everyday situations, with explanations and Quran and authentic hadith references.
difficultyMethod: Editorial classification; not calibrated from learner response data. Advanced means greater reasoning depth within this subject, not a scholarly qualification.

review.referenceCheck: Primary-text references checked during preparation; this is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Handle I am not sure as a UI action, not as a fifth answer option.

questions.question: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 6094, what does truthfulness lead toward?

options.text: Righteousness
A guarantee of popularity
Freedom from all accountability
Permission to mislead when convenient

questions.explanation: The narration connects truthfulness with righteousness and Paradise, and contrasts it with the path of persistent falsehood.

questions.question: What does Quran 4:58 command regarding trusts?

options.text: Keep them if the owner becomes unpopular.
Return them to their rightful owners.
Use them without regard to the agreement.
Return them only when other people are watching.

questions.explanation: The verse joins fulfilling trusts with judging fairly between people.

questions.question: What does Quran 17:34 say about commitments?

options.text: Treat them as irrelevant once inconvenient.
Keep only those made in public.
Fulfil them; they will be asked about.
Assume no commitment creates responsibility.

questions.explanation: Al-Isra 17:34 emphasizes fulfilling commitments and accountability for them.

questions.question: According to Quran 4:135, justice must be upheld even against whom?

options.text: Only people from another town
Only strangers who are poor
Only people with no influence
Oneself, parents or close relatives

questions.explanation: The verse makes family connection and personal interest insufficient reasons to distort testimony.

questions.question: What warning does Quran 5:8 give about hatred of a people?

options.text: Do not let it lead to injustice.
It removes their right to fair treatment.
It makes every accusation against them true.
It replaces the need for evidence.

questions.explanation: Al-Maidah 5:8 commands justice despite hostility and connects justice with mindfulness of Allah.

questions.question: In Quran 49:6, what should believers do when a wrongdoer brings news?

options.text: Spread it because it is surprising.
Verify it before causing harm in ignorance.
Treat emotion as sufficient proof.
Punish the accused before checking.

questions.explanation: The verse links verification with avoiding ignorant harm and later regret.

questions.question: What does Quran 49:11 prohibit groups from doing to one another?

options.text: Learning one another's names
Helping one another respectfully
Ridiculing one another
Seeking reconciliation

questions.explanation: The verse prohibits ridicule and reminds people that those mocked may be better than those mocking them.

questions.question: Which practice is prohibited in Quran 49:11 alongside insulting one another?

options.text: Using someone's preferred respectful name
Introducing a new colleague
Learning a difficult pronunciation
Calling one another by offensive nicknames

questions.explanation: The verse warns against degrading labels, not ordinary respectful identification.

questions.question: Which conduct is expressly prohibited in Quran 49:12?

options.text: Spying on one another
Protecting another person's privacy
Declining to repeat a rumour
Checking one's own mistake

questions.explanation: The verse addresses suspicion, spying and backbiting as harmful conduct.

questions.question: How is backbiting explained in Sahih Muslim 2589?

options.text: Any mention of another person's name
Mentioning about a person what they would dislike
Every disagreement over an idea
Only making a statement known to be false

questions.explanation: The narration distinguishes an unwelcome true statement about a person from a false accusation, which is slander.

questions.question: According to Quran 49:13, why were people made into nations and tribes?

options.text: So ancestry alone determines virtue
So one language can claim automatic holiness for its speakers
So they may know one another
So wealthy groups may ignore others' rights

questions.explanation: The verse connects human diversity with mutual recognition and places honour with Allah in taqwa.

questions.question: Which attitude does Quran 31:18 warn against?

options.text: Listening without self-importance
Acknowledging a mistake
Speaking respectfully to a stranger
Arrogantly turning away from people

questions.explanation: Luqman's advice warns against contemptuous behaviour and boastful arrogance.

questions.question: What advice about speech appears in Quran 31:19?

options.text: Lower or moderate one's voice.
Shout to prove every point.
Treat volume as proof of truth.
Avoid every form of conversation.

questions.explanation: The verse encourages moderation in conduct and voice, rather than needless loudness.

questions.question: What manner of speech toward elderly parents is required in Quran 17:23?

options.text: Humiliation whenever care becomes tiring
Respectful speech without contempt or harsh rebuke
Insults if accompanied by financial help
Silence used only to punish them

questions.explanation: The verse prohibits even an expression of irritation and commands honourable speech.

questions.question: In Sahih al-Bukhari 5991, maintaining kinship means more than what?

options.text: Helping a relative in need
Speaking respectfully
Merely returning relatives' good treatment
Making a sincere effort at reconciliation

questions.explanation: The narration praises maintaining family ties even when relatives have severed them, rather than simple reciprocity.

questions.question: What does Jibril's repeated advice in Sahih al-Bukhari 6014 emphasize?

options.text: The automatic transfer of every neighbour's property
Permission to disturb neighbours at night
A rule that neighbours never need help
Kind treatment of neighbours

questions.explanation: The repeated emphasis shows the importance of neighbourly care; the narration does not itself establish an inheritance entitlement.

questions.question: Which conduct toward a guest is taught in Sahih al-Bukhari 6018?

options.text: Honour the guest.
Humiliate the guest publicly.
Demand praise before showing any kindness.
Treat every visitor as an enemy.

questions.explanation: The narration connects faith with honouring guests, responsible speech and avoiding harm to neighbours.

questions.question: What practice is encouraged in Sahih Muslim 54a as a means of fostering love?

options.text: Competing in insults
Spreading the greeting of peace
Avoiding every greeting
Publicly ranking people's wealth

questions.explanation: The narration connects greeting one another with growing mutual love.

questions.question: What does Quran 24:27 require before entering homes other than one's own?

options.text: Enter whenever the door is unlocked.
Announce ownership of anything visible.
Seek permission and greet the occupants.
Assume familiarity removes all privacy.

questions.explanation: The verse teaches respect for the occupants' permission and greeting.

questions.question: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 6245, what should a visitor do if permission is not given after asking three times?

options.text: Enter by another door.
Keep knocking until the occupants surrender.
Look through windows to force a response.
Return.

questions.explanation: The narration describes the instruction to leave after three unsuccessful requests for permission.

questions.question: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 2079, what supports blessing in a transaction?

options.text: Truthfulness and clear disclosure
Concealing defects effectively
Pressuring a buyer with false information
Making a claim no one can check

questions.explanation: The narration contrasts honest disclosure with lies and concealment that remove blessing.

questions.question: In Sahih Muslim 102, what problem did the Prophet expose in a pile of food for sale?

options.text: The seller had made every defect visible.
Wet food had been hidden beneath what buyers could see.
The food had been given away freely.
The seller had refused to make any sale.

questions.explanation: The Prophet questioned the hidden wetness and rebuked deceptive presentation.

questions.question: What act is rewarded in the thirsty-dog account in Sahih al-Bukhari 2363?

options.text: Withholding water to display power
Mocking a suffering animal
Giving water to a thirsty animal
Refusing mercy because it is not a human

questions.explanation: The account teaches that kindness to a living creature can be rewarded.

questions.question: Which employer's conduct receives a grave warning in Sahih al-Bukhari 2270?

options.text: Paying the agreed wage
Clarifying duties before hiring
Thanking someone for honest work
Taking a worker's full labour without paying the wage

questions.explanation: The narration includes withholding the wage after receiving the work among serious wrongs.

questions.question: In Sahih al-Bukhari 6114, what is the measure of real strength?

options.text: Controlling oneself when angry
Winning every physical contest
Always having the final insult
Making everyone fear disagreement

questions.explanation: The narration identifies restraint in anger as strength, rather than simply overpowering another person.

questions.question: Which conduct is prohibited in Sahih al-Bukhari 6065?

options.text: Sincere goodwill
Envy and mutual hatred
Respectful cooperation
Repairing a disagreement

questions.explanation: The report warns against envy, hatred and turning away from one another, and calls for brotherhood.

questions.question: According to Sahih al-Bukhari 2444, how does one help a person who is oppressing others?

options.text: Hide every trace of their wrongdoing.
Give them more victims.
Stop them from committing oppression.
Call their oppression a virtue.

questions.explanation: The Prophet explains that restraining the oppressor is the form of help required.

questions.question: What does Sahih Muslim 2594a teach about gentleness?

options.text: It necessarily makes all correction impossible.
It is useful only when no disagreement exists.
It means concealing every injustice.
It beautifies what it is part of.

questions.explanation: The narration praises gentleness and describes the loss caused by its absence.

questions.question: What does Quran 2:263 describe as better than charity followed by hurt?

options.text: Kind words and forgiveness
A larger audience for the donor
A demand for public gratitude
A humiliating reminder of generosity

questions.explanation: The verse values considerate words and pardon above giving that is followed by injury.

questions.question: According to Quran 60:8, how may Muslims treat those who have not fought them over religion or driven them from their homes?

options.text: With automatic hostility regardless of conduct
With kindness and justice
By denying every agreement with them
By assuming their property has no protection

questions.explanation: The verse expressly permits kindness and justice toward the people it describes.

questions.question: A dramatic accusation about a colleague arrives from an unreliable source. Which response best applies Quran 49:6?

options.text: Forward it because the accusation is serious.
Add stronger language to attract attention.
Check the information before spreading it or acting against them.
Treat the number of forwards as proof.

questions.explanation: The verification principle matters especially when acting on a claim could harm someone.

questions.question: A truthful statement would expose a close friend's wrongdoing. Which response follows Quran 4:135?

options.text: Invent an alternative account as an act of loyalty.
Assume friendship removes accountability.
Let the friend's wealth determine the truth.
Maintain justice instead of changing testimony to protect the friend.

questions.explanation: The verse requires justice even where personal and family interests make it difficult.

questions.question: Someone says an unkind private discussion cannot be backbiting because the information is true. How does Sahih Muslim 2589 answer?

options.text: Truth does not by itself remove backbiting; a false claim would add slander.
Every true statement is automatically harmless.
Backbiting is defined only as a spelling error.
A person's absence makes all claims acceptable.

questions.explanation: The narration's distinction makes truthfulness insufficient as a blanket defence for speaking about someone harmfully.

questions.question: A seller knows a device has a recurring defect that a buyer has not noticed. What best reflects Sahih al-Bukhari 2079?

options.text: Hide it unless the buyer guesses its exact name.
Disclose the defect honestly before completing the sale.
Claim it is new because its case is clean.
Assume a high price removes disclosure duties.

questions.explanation: The narration emphasizes truthfulness and making relevant qualities and defects clear.

questions.question: A member of one's own group is mistreating someone else. What response follows Sahih al-Bukhari 2444?

options.text: Defend the conduct simply because the person belongs to the group.
Blame the victim to preserve the group's image.
Restrain the wrongdoing rather than protect it out of group loyalty.
Assume helping an oppressor means helping the oppression succeed.

questions.explanation: The narration redefines helping the wrongdoer as preventing their wrongdoing.

questions.question: A debtor is genuinely in financial hardship. What does Quran 2:280 instruct?

options.text: Humiliate them as the first response.
Pretend financial hardship never exists.
Increase pressure solely to make an example of them.
Allow time until circumstances improve.

questions.explanation: The verse directs giving respite to a debtor in hardship and also praises charitable remission.

questions.question: Parents pressure their child to associate partners with Allah. What balance appears in Quran 31:15?

options.text: Do not obey that demand, but maintain kind worldly companionship.
Obey because every parental command overrides belief.
Use the disagreement as permission for cruelty.
Assume kindness requires accepting the demand.

questions.explanation: The verse explicitly combines refusal of that demand with good treatment.

questions.question: A visitor receives no answer after asking permission three times. What best respects the instruction in Sahih al-Bukhari 6245?

options.text: Enter because silence always means consent.
Leave without treating access as an entitlement.
Demand that neighbours unlock the house.
Wait at a window to examine the room.

questions.explanation: Respectful visiting includes accepting that permission has not been granted.

questions.question: Someone gives generously but publicly insults the recipient. Which comparison in Quran 2:263 corrects their priorities?

options.text: The size of the gift makes every insult acceptable.
Recipients lose dignity when accepting help.
Kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by hurt.
Public humiliation is a required part of giving.

questions.explanation: The verse refuses to separate the gift from the conduct that follows it.

questions.question: A friend asks for help carrying out a dishonest scheme. Which instruction in Quran 5:2 is relevant?

options.text: Cooperate in any plan if the friendship is old.
Treat loyalty as permission to ignore wrongdoing.
Judge the scheme only by its profit.
Cooperate in righteousness, not sin and aggression.

questions.explanation: The verse distinguishes worthwhile cooperation from assistance in wrongdoing.

questions.question: A merchant demands full measure when buying but gives customers less when selling. Which passage directly addresses this pattern?

options.text: Quran 83:1–3
Quran 97:1–3 about Laylat al-Qadr
Quran 12:4 about Yusuf's dream
Quran 105:1 about the people of the elephant

questions.explanation: Al-Mutaffifin condemns those who claim full measure for themselves but give less to others.

questions.question: A colleague insults someone during a disagreement. What response best reflects the strength praised in Sahih al-Bukhari 6114?

options.text: Find a more humiliating insult immediately.
Control one's reaction and address the issue without an abusive outburst.
Treat loss of control as proof of courage.
Let anger determine every factual claim.

questions.explanation: The narration makes self-control, rather than retaliation, the relevant measure of strength.

questions.question: A group keeps using a nickname after learning that it humiliates the person. Which teaching in Quran 49:11 applies?

options.text: The group's amusement overrides the person's dignity.
A nickname becomes respectful whenever it is popular.
Avoid offensive name-calling.
Humiliation is acceptable if no money is lost.

questions.explanation: The prohibition of degrading names matters even when the speakers call their conduct humour.

questions.question: Someone repeatedly causes avoidable noise that harms neighbours and dismisses their complaints. Which teaching is most directly relevant?

options.text: A claim that worship excuses every disturbance
A rule that neighbours have rights only when related
An assumption that owning a home permits unlimited harm
The instruction not to harm one's neighbour in Sahih al-Bukhari 6018

questions.explanation: The duty to avoid neighbourly harm applies to conduct, not merely polite greetings.

questions.question: A person has wronged someone in their honour or another right. What does Sahih al-Bukhari 2449 urge?

options.text: Seek release from that wrongdoing before the Day when money cannot settle it.
Ignore it because time automatically cancels the right.
Assume public reputation removes responsibility.
Wait until the harmed person forgets every detail.

questions.explanation: The narration emphasizes addressing another person's claim rather than postponing accountability indefinitely.

questions.question: In Sahih Muslim 2581, a person arrives with prayer, fasting and charity but has harmed others. What does the account of bankruptcy establish?

options.text: Prayer gives unrestricted permission to insult people.
Acts of worship do not make violations of others' rights morally irrelevant.
Only financial poverty can count as bankruptcy.
Harming others always increases one's good deeds.

questions.explanation: The narration describes good deeds being transferred to those wronged, showing the gravity of interpersonal injustice.

questions.question: Someone cites the prohibition of harmful speech to silence a person seeking help after being wronged. Which qualification in Quran 4:148 matters?

options.text: The verse says every accusation is true.
The verse prohibits every request for protection.
The verse makes an exception concerning the person who has been wronged.
The verse requires victims to praise harmful conduct.

questions.explanation: The exception prevents a blanket use of speech ethics to silence the wronged; it does not authorize invented allegations or unlimited disclosure.

questions.question: Read together, what balance appears in Quran 42:40–43?

options.text: The wronged person is always blameworthy for seeking any redress.
Pardon requires declaring the wrongdoing good.
Any response may exceed the original wrong without limit.
Pardon is praised, while seeking redress after being wronged is not itself blamed; wrongdoing remains blameworthy.

questions.explanation: The passage distinguishes proportionate response, pardon and reconciliation from oppression and transgression.

questions.question: A person obtains a favourable judgment by presenting a deceptive but persuasive case. What warning appears in Sahih al-Bukhari 2680?

options.text: A judgment based on what is heard does not make another person's right lawful to take.
A persuasive presentation changes falsehood into truth.
Every successful claimant is necessarily morally innocent.
The person who speaks longest owns the disputed property.

questions.explanation: The Prophet warns that a judgment obtained at another's expense does not remove the underlying injustice.

questions.question: A family asks someone to distort evidence to protect a relative and calls it family duty. What distinction follows from Quran 4:135?

options.text: A family relationship automatically outranks justice.
Family loyalty does not authorize false testimony or injustice.
Evidence should be changed whenever it prevents embarrassment.
Justice applies only when no relative is involved.

questions.explanation: The verse expressly includes difficult cases involving oneself, parents and relatives.

questions.question: Someone rejects a valid claim solely because it comes from a disliked community. How does Quran 5:8 challenge this?

options.text: Dislike is conclusive evidence that the claim is false.
Justice is reserved for people one trusts personally.
Hostility cannot replace fair judgment of the claim.
A group's unpopularity removes every member's rights.

questions.explanation: The command to remain just constrains the effect of personal or communal hostility.

questions.question: Does Quran 49:6 justify declaring every unfamiliar person a liar without investigation?

options.text: Yes; unfamiliarity alone proves wrongdoing.
Yes; lack of a public profile establishes dishonesty.
No; the verse instead says never verify any news.
No; the verification instruction is not a licence for unsupported accusations.

questions.explanation: The verse requires care before harmful action; inventing an accusation while claiming to verify would defeat that care.

questions.question: Which conclusion best preserves both parts of Quran 31:15 when parents demand association of partners with Allah?

options.text: Refuse that demand while retaining kind treatment; refusal and cruelty are different matters.
Kindness requires obeying the demand.
Refusal permits every form of humiliation.
The verse abolishes all parent-child responsibilities.

questions.explanation: The verse places a limit on obedience without removing the instruction of good companionship.

questions.question: Why is 'the information is true' insufficient by itself to justify sharing a person's embarrassing details widely?

options.text: Every true statement about a person is forbidden in all circumstances.
Truth does not settle whether disclosure has a legitimate purpose, proper scope or involves backbiting.
A person's absence makes all disclosure harmless.
Sharing more widely always makes the information more accurate.

questions.explanation: Sahih Muslim 2589 shows that truth alone does not remove backbiting; Quran 4:148 also requires attention to the context of a wronged person speaking.

questions.question: A mediator wants to stop a dispute by asking the weaker party to accept continuing oppression. What feature of Quran 49:9–10 challenges this?

options.text: The larger group is automatically right.
Every settlement is just merely because it ends public argument.
Reconciliation is joined with justice and equitable treatment.
Justice becomes irrelevant once mediation begins.

questions.explanation: The passage calls for reconciliation without presenting oppression as an acceptable basis for peace.

questions.question: An employer advertises generous charity while withholding a worker's earned wage. What distinction is essential?

options.text: Public charity automatically cancels wage obligations.
A worker's right depends entirely on public approval.
A donor may transfer all employment duties to the charity recipient.
Voluntary generosity does not excuse denying an existing right.

questions.explanation: The warning in Sahih al-Bukhari 2270 concerns unpaid labour; the account of bankruptcy in Sahih Muslim 2581 shows that worship and giving do not erase interpersonal wrongdoing.

questions.question: Someone says all kindness toward non-Muslims is prohibited regardless of their conduct. Which limitation in Quran 60:8 is crucial?

options.text: It expressly permits kindness and justice toward those not fighting the believers over religion or expelling them.
It prohibits justice toward every outsider.
It makes kindness depend solely on shared ancestry.
It says every treaty removes all moral duties.

questions.explanation: The verse's stated permission refutes an indiscriminate prohibition; the question does not attempt to define every political relationship.

questions.question: After a disagreement, someone wants to keep property entrusted to them purely to punish its owner. What principle in Quran 4:58 applies?

options.text: Every dispute automatically transfers ownership.
An entrusted item remains due to its rightful owner; personal anger does not by itself cancel the trust.
The more offended party may seize any entrusted property.
A private punishment creates a lawful title without evidence.

questions.explanation: The instruction to return trusts is not made conditional on continued personal affection. A separate legal claim should not be invented from anger.

questions.question: A friend says restraining their wrongdoing is disloyal. Which pair of teachings most directly challenges that?

options.text: Honour guests and memorize a calendar date.
Seek permission to enter and change one's clothing.
Help the oppressor by stopping oppression, and do not cooperate in sin or aggression.
Lower one's voice and assume all plans are lawful.

questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari 2444 and Quran 5:2 make moral limits part of support, rather than treating support as unconditional assistance.

questions.question: Someone interprets humility as having to agree with every unfair demand. Which combined reading is more careful?

options.text: Humility makes all evidence unnecessary.
Justice is forbidden whenever speaking may be uncomfortable.
Rejecting injustice necessarily proves arrogance.
Avoid arrogance while still upholding justice and returning people their rights.

questions.explanation: Quran 31:18 condemns arrogant conduct, while Quran 4:58 still commands justice. Humility concerns how one conducts oneself and does not cancel that duty.
